notes: SHIP v1.14.442 - R1-D: THE RACK COMES ABOVE THE FOLD IN FIELD MODE. THE DEFECT, MEASURED NOT DESCRIBED. On a 390x844 phone at .441 the Build rack preview mount started at y=857 against a bottom nav at y=733. VISIBLE PIXELS OF RACK: ZERO. The renderer was healthy the entire time - .441 had already proven the mount holds a live 652x640 WebGL context - so the rack was drawing perfectly into a box the technician could not see without scrolling. 'The rack preview is not working' and 'the rack preview is 124px below the visible area' produce the same report from a cold aisle, which is why this was found by measuring the layout rather than by debugging the renderer. WHAT WAS PUSHING IT DOWN, measured inside the card: header 46px, then a 58px control strip holding exactly ONE chip reading NO CABLE DATA, then a 109px view rail wrapped onto two rows (the disclosed defect D-4). 237px of controls sat between the top of the card and the rack, and the NEXT ACTION card sat above the whole thing. THE FIX DELETES NOTHING. Three changes, all layout. FIRST, the preview card becomes a flex column and its children are ordered so the rack comes directly under the card header and every control group - the cable strip and the full FRONT/ISO/TOP/REAR/CABLES/EXPLODE rail - moves BELOW the rack. Contract 49 is intact: not one control was removed to win the space, and captioning the rack from underneath is the more natural reading order anyway. Flex order rather than a DOM move on purpose, because rackElevation_render3D locates the .reh-3d-toggle strip by querySelector and appends its rail to that strip's PARENT, so re-parenting in JavaScript would fight the renderer; ordering leaves every renderer assumption untouched. Every rule is scoped inside .bw-prev, so the rack-detail panel's own copies of those controls are unaffected. SECOND, the NEXT ACTION card is still built in exactly the same place and with exactly the same content, and is appended after the preview instead of before it - it is one card of derived text, and the rack is what the technician came to look at. THIRD, the hero's internal margins tighten on phone and tablet only: 77px of internal margin around 249px of content. No type size moves, no content is removed, the rack ID and platform chips and phase and progress and CONTINUE all stay exactly as they were, and the 44px tap floors are untouched because --bw-cta is a min-height and not a margin. The desktop grid composition at >=1024 is deliberately excluded - it has no fold problem and its own rules would fight this one. RESULT ON THE MEASURED VIEWPORT: mount top 857 to 557, visible rack 0px to 176px, canvas live at 652x640, OPEN AISLE still above the fold at y=545, CONTINUE and the s4:099 rack identity still above the fold, and no horizontal overflow. NOT YET AT THE DIRECTIVE'S RECOMMENDATION, STATED PLAINLY. Section 30 of the renderer directive recommends 270 to 320px of visible rack. This ship reaches 176. The arithmetic is exact: 651px of column exists above the fold, and with every current block intact the content above the rack costs 475 of it. Reaching 270 needs another 94px, and the only block big enough is the hero, whose phase sub-block (PHASE 3 OF 5, the phase name and the progress bar) is the same fact already shown by the NEXT ACTION card and again by the phase dock at the bottom of the screen. Removing a triplicated fact is a product decision, not a layout one, so it is reported and left to the owner rather than taken unilaterally. The camera term is the other lever and is the one term the RACK SCENE LOCK leaves open - tighter framing would put more rack in the same 176px - but that changes established visual identity and was explicitly excluded from this permission. NO SCENE CHANGE. No material, light, geometry, fog, tone-mapping, floor or colour edit. The rack renders exactly as it did at .441; only where it sits on the page changed. TESTS: new spec 30-rack-above-the-fold, four tests, PROVEN TO CATCH THE DEFECT - with the fix stashed it fails reporting mountTop 857 against a fold at 733. It asserts a visible-pixel FLOOR rather than a bare greater-than-zero, because 1px of rack would satisfy the latter and is not a visible rack; it asserts both control groups survive and both now sit below the mount, so the space can never be won by deleting a capability; it asserts OPEN AISLE and CONTINUE did not fall below the fold, because trading one below-the-fold problem for another is not a fix; and it asserts no horizontal overflow. The spec skips at >=1024 where the desktop shell stands the bottom nav down and there is no fold to measure. RUNS: 30 = 8 passed and 8 skipped across phone, tablet, laptop and desktop. 06-composition + 29 + 26 + 27 + 25 + 01 + 00 on phone = 51 passed. 02-build-forge alone = 14 passed. 06-composition on desktop-chromium = 11 passed, confirming the desktop grid is untouched. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, 12 style blocks brace-balanced, 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep at .442. DEVICE-VERIFY: open BUILD with an active rack and do not scroll. PASS is seeing the rack itself above the phase bar, with the rack ID, CONTINUE and OPEN AISLE all still on screen. FAIL is an empty preview area, or having to scroll to find the rack.
